From today's featured article
Thomas Hardy
(13
September 1666
– 16
August 1732) was a
Royal Navy
officer and politician. In 1702, he was given command of
HMS
Pembroke
and fought at the
Battle of Cádiz
and the
Battle of Vigo Bay
, where he was
knighted
for his services. In 1707, Hardy was sent as escort to a convoy sailing for Lisbon where he met the squadron of
René Duguay-Trouin
. Hardy became
first captain
to
John Leake
in the Mediterranean in 1708, assisting in the transport of
Elisabeth Christine
to Spain for her marriage to
Archduke Charles
, and participating in the capture of
Cagliari
and the
assault on Minorca
. He was promoted to
rear-admiral
and given command of a squadron to blockade
Dunkirk
. After briefly serving as
commander-in-chief, the Nore, Thames and Medway
, Hardy commanded a squadron off
Ushant
where he failed to intercept the squadrons of Duguay-Trouin and
Jean-Baptiste du Casse
. In 1715, he was second-in-command of the
Baltic Fleet
sent to serve in the
Great Northern War
, but he was dismissed in 1716.

Today's featured picture
The
salema porgy
(
Sarpa salpa
) is a species of marine
ray-finned fish
in the seabream and porgy family,
Sparidae
. It has a silvery body with eight to ten horizontal golden lines and a black spot at the base of the
pectoral fin
, and can sometimes reach more than 50
cm (20
in) in length. The species occurs in the eastern Atlantic from the
Bay of Biscay
to South Africa, as well as the Mediterranean Sea, at depths of up to 70
m (230
ft). It is largely herbivorous, feeding principally on seagrasses and algae, and is a
protandrous hermaphrodite
, changing from male to female. Consumption can sometimes cause
ichthyoallyeinotoxism
poisoning, resulting in auditory and visual hallucinations. This salema porgy was photographed in
Catania
, Sicily, Italy.
